A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

The reports are published per facility. They also exclude mice, rats and birds bred for research, which are the overwhelming majority — so the most detailed animal-use record in the United States omits most of the animals.

There is no inspectorate, no declaration anybody checks and no laboratory network — nothing resembling the machinery that exists for nuclear or chemical weapons. The gap is the point of this entry.

2.77000,42.08000.name: HIPRA

2.77000,42.08000.desc: A Spanish animal health company founded in 1971, present in forty countries with subsidiaries and distributing to more than a hundred, running autogenous vaccine plants in Spain and Brazil including a service for farmed fish. This map generally separates the animal and human facets; the manufacturers do not.
